# 1. Effects of Beta Diversity and Spatial Extent on Spatial Asynchrony

```{r import model 1}
model.SA<-readRDS("../04_bayesian_analysis/models/SA_quantile.rds")
```

## 1.1 Prior specification

<br>

**Tabe S1: Prior distributions used in the Bayesian model with normalized spatial asynchrony as the response variable.** All parameters were assigned the default prior specification implemented in brms (prior = "default"). The Student-t prior on the group-level standard deviation was truncated at zero.

```{r, echo=FALSE}

priors_SA_raw <- prior_summary(model.SA) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(
    across(
      c(prior, class, coef, group),
      ~ tidyr::replace_na(as.character(.x), "")
    )
  )

default_b_prior_SA <- priors_SA_raw |>
  filter(class == "b", coef == "", group == "") |>
  pull(prior) |>
  first()

default_sd_prior_SA <- priors_SA_raw |>
  filter(class == "sd", coef == "", group == "") |>
  pull(prior) |>
  first()

prior_table_SA <- priors_SA_raw |>
  filter(
    (class == "b" & coef != "") |
      class %in% c("Intercept", "phi", "zi") |
      (class == "sd" & group == "div" & coef == "Intercept")
  ) |>

  mutate(
    prior = case_when(
      class == "b" & prior == "" & default_b_prior_SA != "" ~
        default_b_prior_SA,
      class == "b" & prior == "" ~
        "(flat)",
      class == "sd" & prior == "" ~
        default_sd_prior_SA,
      TRUE ~ prior
    ),

    `Parameter class` = case_when(
      class == "b"         ~ "Regression coefficient",
      class == "Intercept" ~ "Intercept",
      class == "sd"        ~ "Group-level standard deviation",
      class == "phi"       ~ "Precision parameter",
      class == "zi"        ~ "Zero-inflation parameter"
    ),

    Parameter = case_when(
      coef == "Area"          ~ "Spatial extent",
      coef == "Beta_div"      ~ "β-diversity",
      coef == "Beta_div:Area" ~ "β-diversity × spatial extent",
      class == "Intercept"    ~ "Intercept",
      class == "sd"           ~
        "Planted species richness random intercept",
      class == "phi"          ~ "φ",
      class == "zi"           ~ "Zero-inflation probability"
    ),

    `Prior distribution` = case_when(
      prior == "(flat)" ~ "flat",
      TRUE ~ prior
    ),

    row_order = case_when(
      class == "b" & coef == "Area"          ~ 1,
      class == "b" & coef == "Beta_div"      ~ 2,
      class == "b" & coef == "Beta_div:Area" ~ 3,
      class == "Intercept"                   ~ 4,
      class == "sd"                          ~ 5,
      class == "phi"                         ~ 6,
      class == "zi"                          ~ 7
    )
  ) |>

  arrange(row_order) |>

  select(
    `Parameter class`,
    Parameter,
    `Prior distribution`
  )

knitr::kable(
  prior_table_SA,
  align = c("l", "l", "l")
)

```

<br>

## 1.2 Model and convergence diagnostics 

<br>

**Table S2: Summary table of the BRMS model results.** The table summarizes the posterior distributions of the fixed effects and interaction terms. Reported values include the posterior means, standard errors, 95% credible intervals (CI), and effective sample sizes (Bulk ESS and Tail ESS) for each parameter.

```{r warning=FALSE}
print(model.SA, digits = 3)
```

Note the `Rhat` summary column: variation from 1.0 indicates the the model did not converge.

The Bayesian R-squared:
```{r}
bayes_R2(model.SA)
```

<br>

```{r message=FALSE}
mcmc_trace(as.array(model.SA)) + 
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = function(x) seq(min(x), max(x), length.out = 3),  # Show 3 ticks
    labels = function(x) sprintf("%.1f", x)  # Format ticks to 1 decimal place
  )
```

**Figure S1: Trace plots allow visually assessing chain convergence.**

<br>

## 1.3 Assessment of model fit and accuracy

### 1.3.1 Posterior predictive checks

We assess model fit using posterior predictive checks (PPC). PPCs compare the real data to the posterior distribution, conditioned on the observed data.

#### 1.3.1.1 Density plot

```{r}
pp_check(model.SA, ndraws = 500) + 
  theme_bw() + 
  xlab("Normalized Spatial Asynchrony") +
  ylab("Density")
```

**Figure S2: The density plot compares the real data (`y`, dark blue line) to the fitted draws of the models (`y_rep`, light blue lines).**

<br>

#### 1.3.1.3 Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation

```{r warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, results='hide'}
pp_check(model.SA, type="loo_pit_qq")+ 
  theme_bw() 
```

**Figure S3: The LOO-PIT (Leave-One-Out Probability Integral Transform) calibration plot compares the empirical cumulative distribution of the LOO-PIT values (solid blue line) against the uniform distribution (dashed diagonal line).**

<br>

### 1.3.2 Highest-density interval

We report 89% instead of 95% following common Bayesian practices, as it provides a better balance of precision and interpretability (McElreath, 2020).

```{r message=FALSE}
my.hdi.1 <- hdi(model.SA, ci = 0.89)
new_labels <- c( #create a vector with new parameter names that reflect the terminology of the ms
  "b_Beta_div" = "Beta Diversity",
  "b_Area" = "Spatial Extent",
  "b_Beta_div:Area" = "Beta Diversity x Spatial Extent"
)

  plot(my.hdi.1)+
  scale_y_discrete(labels = new_labels) # adjust labels

```

**Figure S4: We use the highest density interval (HDI) for the main effects in the model to characterize uncertainty of our posterior distributions.** 

<br>

## 1.4 The Hierarchical Effect of Species Richness on Spatial Asynchrony

<br>

**Table S3: Summary table of the hierarchical effects of planted species richness on spatial asynchrony.**

```{r}
ranef(model.SA)
```

<br>

```{r}
model.SA %>% spread_draws(r_div[div,]) %>% # Extracts the posterior draws for r_div by each level of div
  ungroup() %>%
  compare_levels(r_div, by = div) %>% # Compares posterior distributions of r_div across div levels
  ggplot(aes(y = div, x = r_div)) +
  stat_halfeye() +  # Adds a half-eye plot (density + credible intervals)
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +  # Adds a dashed vertical reference line at x = 0
  # Axis labels
  xlab("Posterior Random Effect Value") +
  ylab("Levels of Planted Spcies\nRichness") +
  # Plot aesthetics
  theme(axis.title = element_text(size = 20, colour = "black"), #to modify axes appearance
        axis.line.x = element_line(colour = "black"),
        axis.line.y = element_line(colour = "black"),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 15,colour="black"),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 15,colour="black"),
        legend.text  = element_text(size = 15,colour="black"),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 20,colour="black"),
        legend.key.width = unit(1, "cm"),  # Increase legend key width to show linetypes clearly
        strip.text = element_text(size = 20),
        axis.ticks = element_line(colour="black"),
        panel.border = element_rect(colour="black", fill=NA))

```

**Figure S5: Posterior distributions of the random effects of planted species richness levels on spatial asynchrony, comparing differences between species richness levels.** Black points represent posterior medians, and horizontal black lines indicate the 66% and 95% credible intervals. The dashed vertical line at x = 0 serves as a reference for no difference. Deviations from zero indicate the magnitude and direction of the differences in spatial asynchrony between species richness levels.

# 2. Effects of Spatial Asynchony and Spatial Extent on Gamma Stability

```{r import model 2}
model.GS<-readRDS("../04_bayesian_analysis/models/GS_quantile.rds")
```

## 2.1 Prior Specification

<br>

**Table S4: Prior distributions used in the Bayesian model with gamma stability as the response variable.** All parameters were assigned the default prior specification implemented in brms (prior = "default"). Student-t priors on the group-level and residual standard deviation parameters were truncated at zero.

```{r}

priors_gamma_raw <- prior_summary(model.GS) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(
    across(
      c(prior, class, coef, group),
      ~ replace_na(as.character(.x), "")))

# Extract the class-level priors that specific parameters inherit
default_b_prior <- priors_gamma_raw |>
  filter(class == "b", coef == "", group == "") |>
  pull(prior) |>
  first()

default_sd_prior <- priors_gamma_raw |>
  filter(class == "sd", coef == "", group == "") |>
  pull(prior) |>
  first()

prior_table_gamma <- priors_gamma_raw |>
  filter(
    (class == "b" & coef != "") |
      class %in% c("Intercept", "sigma") |
      (class == "sd" & group == "div" & coef == "Intercept")) |>

  mutate(
    # Fill specific rows with their inherited class-level priors
    prior = case_when(
  class == "b" & prior == "" & default_b_prior != "" ~ default_b_prior,
  class == "b" & prior == ""                         ~ "(flat)",
  class == "sd" & prior == ""                        ~ default_sd_prior,
  TRUE                                               ~ prior),

    `Parameter class` = case_when(
      class == "b"         ~ "Regression parameter",
      class == "Intercept" ~ "Intercept",
      class == "sd"        ~ "Group-level standard deviation",
      class == "sigma"     ~ "Residual standard deviation"),

    Parameter = case_when(
      coef == "Area"            ~ "Spatial extent",
      coef == "Spatial_AS"      ~ "Spatial asynchrony",
      coef == "Spatial_AS:Area" ~
        "Spatial asynchrony × spatial extent",
      class == "Intercept"      ~ "Intercept",
      class == "sd"             ~
        "Planted species richness random intercept",
      class == "sigma"          ~ "σ"),

    `Prior distribution` = case_when(
      prior == "(flat)" ~ "flat",
      TRUE              ~ prior),

    row_order = case_when(
      class == "b" & coef == "Area"            ~ 1,
      class == "b" & coef == "Spatial_AS"      ~ 2,
      class == "b" & coef == "Spatial_AS:Area" ~ 3,
      class == "Intercept"                     ~ 4,
      class == "sd"                            ~ 5,
      class == "sigma"                         ~ 6)) |>

  arrange(row_order) |>

  select(
    `Parameter class`,
    Parameter,
    `Prior distribution`)

knitr::kable(
  prior_table_gamma,
  align = c("l", "l", "l"))

```

<br>
